section.title: The ooSQLCollationNeeded Class
section.para: An ooSQLCollationNeeded object represents the collation needed callback of an ooSQLite package: a function, written in C or C++, that SQLite invokes when a statement uses a collation that the connection does not have, so that it can register it. A package has at most one. The C code stays in the shared library of the package; the object holds what ooSQLite needs to register it: its name and its entry points. Programs do not create ooSQLCollationNeeded objects: ooSQLite creates them.

The object is obtained with the getCollationNeeded method of an ooSQLPackage object, and its only use is as the argument of the collationNeeded method of the ooSQLiteConnection class, which also accepts the package itself. The same object can be registered on any number of connections. autoCollationNeeded makes it automatic.

row.entry: Creates the object. Used internally by ooSQLite.

section.title: new (Class method)
section.para: Creates an ooSQLCollationNeeded object. ooSQLite uses it internally; programs obtain the object with the getCollationNeeded method of an ooSQLPackage object.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
entry [required]
A Buffer object with a copy of the description that the package gives in C. Only ooSQLite can create it.
A Rexx program can not create the Buffer object that new needs, so new invoked from a program raises a syntax error: 88.901 without an argument, and 88.900 with any other argument.

&changed11;A subclass of ooSQLCollationNeeded whose init method does not forward to the init method of ooSQLCollationNeeded creates objects that are not initialized. collationNeeded raises an execution error, 98.900, when it is given one. Before ooSQLite 1.1 it crashed the interpreter.

The testPackage package, which is built with the examples, has a collation needed callback that registers its collations when SQLite asks for them:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('testpackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('testPackage') needed = package~getCollationNeeded say needed say db~collationNeeded(needed) sql = "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES ('a'), ('c'), ('b'))" - "SELECT group_concat(x, ' ') AS v FROM (SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE reverseOrder);" say db~exec(sql, .true)[1]['V'] /* Output: an ooSQLCollationNeeded 0 c b a */
